newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 26.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- MOBILE PHONES TARGET OFFICES

Vodafone yesterday introduced a dual phone system. Contracts were placed with Ericsson for base station equipment to allow mobile phones to be used inside offices. Companies will have to buy new handsets to allow phones to operate inside and outside the office, on different frequencies. Cellnet, British Telecom and Securicor mobile phone operators are all set to announce plans to move into the market that has opened up since the Government's decision to allocate more of the radio spectrum to allow companies to tap new markets.
-- ALCOPOPS DRAIN CIDER PROFITS

Merrydown, the cider maker, yesterday blamed its falling profits on the launch of over 90 new products into the alcopops market since its own Two Dogs alcoholic lemonade arrived from Australia last year. Merrydown's interim pre-tax profit was down 42 per cent for the six months ending September 30.
-- FIRSTBUS ON LOOKOUT FOR MORE TARGETS AS PROFITS LEAP 81 PER CENT

Britain's biggest local bus company, FirstBus announced yesterday that it is looking overseas for acquisitions after revealing an 81 per cent rise in first-half, pre-tax profits to 25.7 million pounds stg. This year, FirstBus, has spent 194 million pounds stg on British acquisitions including Greater Manchester Buses and Strathclyde Buses and both are performing ahead of expectations.
THE TIMES
-- ROSYTH SAVED BY 500 MILLION POUNDS ORDER ON SALE TO BABCOCK

Rosyth Royal Dockyard was finally sold to Babcock International after two and a half years of negotiations between the Ministry of Defence and Babcock, who have managed the dockyard since 1987. Defence Secretary Michael Portillo announced firm orders for refitting some of the Royal Navy's most prestigious warships at the dockyard. The work will last ten years, and be worth 500 million pounds stg.
-- AMEY AND McALPINE WIN 175 MILLION POUNDS CONTRACT

The contract to build the Croydon Tramlink system, was yesterday awarded to Amey and Sir Robert McAlpine. The 175 million pounds stg contract is one of the first projects of its kind since the disappearance of trams in the London area in the early 1950s. The two construction companies will design, construct and maintain the 17-mile light rail network.
-- PAPERLESS DEADLINE REMAINS AT CREST

The board of CrestCo decided unanimously yesterday to press on with its timetable for full conversion to paperless trading in the city, by April. Stockbrokers are increasingly worried that Crest will cause delays to thousands of investors, but the board decided it is in the entire market's interest that the transition period is completed as quickly as possible.
THE GUARDIAN
-- SALVESEN DENOUNCED FOR 150 MILLION POUNDS 'GIVEAWAY'

Sir Gerald Elliot, family shareholder and a former chairman of Christian Salvesen, yesterday denounced the transport group's plans to distribute 150 million pounds stg to shareholders calling it "destructive manipulations for the benefit of stock exchange punters". Salvesen investors will get dividends worth around 54.8p a share made up from the payment of a 50 million pounds stg "enhanced dividend", with a further 100 million pounds stg "foreign income dividend".
-- LLOYDS CHEMIST HIT BY ETHICS ROW

It emerged yesterday that directors of Lloyds Chemist restructured their pay packages in advance of fresh takeover bids. Institutional investors unhappy with boardroom ethics are considering bringing the matter up at the annual meeting of the company due to take place today.
-- TAKEOVER ROCKS SWEDISH POLITICS

Plans for a 2 billion pounds stg merger in Sweden has caused a high-level row. The proposed takeover by insurance group Skania of mortgage bank Stadshypotek, in which the Swedish government has a 34 per cent stake, came under attack from finance minister Eric Asbrink who found it remarkable that the board of Stadshypotek have gone ahead with the merger proposals knowing that the government was set to sell its holding.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- PRE-BUDGET CELEBRATION SENDS STERLING AND SHARES SOARING

The pound rose to its highest level since sterling left the Exchange Rate Mechanism over four years ago due to advance celebrations of the Budget. Shares rose to within reach of their all-time high. Kenneth Clarke's statement yesterday that there was no question of sterling shadowing the Euro also helped lift the pound. Hope that the Budget would be cautious enough to prevent another rise in interest rates took the FT-SE 100 index of share prices to 4,054.6 yesterday, up 36 points.
-- FIRE COULD LEAVE EUROTUNNEL WITH 165 MILLION POUNDS BILL

The cost of last week's fire in the Channel Tunnel could be as much as 165 million pounds stg, with Eurotunnel picking up the bill, if the fire prevents full service resuming for the next three months as senior executives now fear. This figure does not include repair of the damage as this should be covered by insurance and it does not include the long-term costs if the company is forced into extensive modifications to the design of the freight shuttles.
-- ANDERSON CONFIRMS ROLE IN FOREST CONSORTIUM

The head of Porterbrook Leasing, Sandy Anderson, confirmed yesterday his lead role in a consortium bidding for control of Nottingham Forest football club. It is believed that if the bid is successful, Anderson will take on executive duties at Forest, even as chief executive. The consortium also includes Charles Scott, head of Coridiant and Nigel Doughty-Hanson of Doughty & Hanson.
